articles.summary: Jay-Z says he feels no pressure about headlining the Super Bowl 61 halftime show.
articles.body: Jay-Z says he feels no pressure about headlining the Super Bowl 61 halftime show. The 56-year-old rapper was asked about it by TMZ in New York City on Tuesday, October 27, a day after Apple Music’s Monday Night Football broadcast announced him as the performer. The show is set for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. It will be his first halftime appearance on stage, though his company, Roc Nation, has produced the event since 2019. His answers were brief, and he gave them with a smile.Jay-Z says there is no pressure ahead of halftime showTMZ’s photographer asked the obvious question first. Did he feel any pressure? Jay-Z kept it short. “No pressure,” he said.The follow-up was about preparation. “Same as always,” he replied. No hint about the setlist, surprise guests or production, which is exactly what fans want to know right now. The silence fits him, though. This is a man who has sold out arenas for decades and built a billion-dollar business empire along the way. From someone with that résumé, a one-line answer sounds less like dodging and more like a shrug.Still, the Super Bowl is not a regular tour stop. Halftime reaches people who would never buy a concert ticket, and every song choice gets picked apart online within minutes. His calm suggests he will not change his approach just because the audience got bigger.Roger Goodell says Jay-Z picked his own momentNFL commissioner Roger Goodell added context on The Ebro Show on Tuesday. The league has wanted this for years, he said, and he first raised it when the partnership began.“We’ve always wanted this to happen at some point. It was something I asked him about at the time when we first started this, and he said, ‘Yeah, we’ll see. Let’s see what happens.’ But it was clear he wanted it to happen,” Goodell explained.The timing, he said, came from Jay-Z. “I think the fact that he’s in his 30th anniversary year of his first album, he just finished his tour, it’s L.A., he’s at that point as the GOAT that he’s ready for it,” Goodell said. He added that Jay-Z was direct about it. “I guess I was more excited than anything, maybe a little surprised, because he keeps putting it off a little bit.”The twist is hard to miss. Roc Nation has produced the halftime show since 2019, and the NFL extended that deal in 2024. The person who helped shape recent lineups is now the one on stage.He follows a busy run. SoFi hosted Super Bowl 56 in 2022 with Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige and Kendrick Lamar. Rihanna, Usher, Lamar again and Bad Bunny have headlined since. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ brand owner seeks an injunction against My Chemical Romance after lookalike dancers appeared in a staged Hollywood Bowl gunfight
articles.summary: My Chemical Romance is facing a legal challenge from the company behind the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders over dancers wearing lookalike uniforms during the
articles.body: My Chemical Romance is facing a legal challenge from the company behind the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders over dancers wearing lookalike uniforms during the rock band’s Hollywood Bowl residency in Los Angeles. According to reports by NBC News, NME and TheWrap, Pro Silver Star Ltd., the owner of the cheerleading brand, has asked a Texas court to prevent the band from continuing to use the costumes in its performances. The dispute centres on a theatrical sequence in which dancers dressed in outfits resembling the cheerleaders’ distinctive blue-and-white uniforms took part in a staged gunfight. The company argues that the use of its recognisable branding in a violent performance could damage the reputation and commercial value of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.What happened during the Hollywood Bowl performance?The controversy began during My Chemical Romance’s October 21, 2026, performance at the Hollywood Bowl, where the band is celebrating the 20th anniversary of its landmark album The Black Parade. During the song Teenagers, dancers appeared in costumes resembling the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ uniforms. The performance continued into Disenchanted, when the dancers became involved in a choreographed confrontation with soldiers, carrying prop rifles before appearing to be shot and crawling offstage.The sequence formed part of the band’s theatrical presentation for its anniversary tour. However, the resemblance between the costumes and the professional cheerleading squad’s signature outfits has now become the focus of a legal dispute. Pro Silver Star maintains that the costumes could lead audiences to believe the performers were official members of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. The company has pointed to social media reactions as evidence that some viewers made that connection.Brand owner alleges trademark infringementPro Silver Star filed its request for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction on October 23, seeking to stop the band from using the disputed uniforms. The company contends that the outfits reproduce distinctive elements of the cheerleaders’ established look, including white boots, white shorts, blue cropped tops and white vests decorated with blue stars, according to reporting by the Los Angeles Times and TheWrap. The dispute goes beyond costume similarities. The company argues that using recognisable uniforms in a simulated shooting sequence risks associating the real cheerleading squad with violence, potentially harming its reputation and commercial goodwill.Pro Silver Star also alleges that it approached the band about discontinuing the costumes before turning to the courts. Footage from the October 23 concert appeared to show dancers wearing similar outfits again, according to NME and Rolling Stone. The company is seeking unspecified monetary damages alongside the requested court order. The legal action raises questions about the limits of trademark protection for recognisable uniforms when they are incorporated into artistic performances.My Chemical Romance’s anniversary tour continuesThe legal dispute comes as My Chemical Romance marks two decades of The Black Parade, the band’s influential 2006 album that helped establish its place in alternative rock. The Hollywood Bowl residency is part of the group’s Long Live The Black Parade tour, which features the album performed in full alongside a theatrical narrative built around a fictional authoritarian regime. The staged confrontation involving the dancers fits into that broader production rather than functioning as a standalone performance.The band had further Hollywood Bowl dates scheduled for October 30 and 31, bringing its five-show residency to a close. Whether the disputed costumes would appear in those performances remained uncertain at the time of reporting. Neither My Chemical Romance nor its representatives had publicly responded to media requests for comment, according to reports published by NBC News and TheWrap. The request for an injunction is a legal claim, not a final finding of infringement, and the outcome will depend on the court proceedings.For now, the case places a familiar tension between artistic expression and brand protection in the spotlight. Pro Silver Star’s position is that the band can retain its music, staging and storyline while changing the costumes. The central question is whether the lookalike outfits cross the legal line from theatrical reference to unauthorised use of a protected commercial identity.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 76ers’ VJ Edgecombe somehow nails 1st-half buzzer-beater before the logo
articles.summary: That’s one way to close the halftime. The Philadelphia 76ers played the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night as VJ Edgecombe gave the Sixers a highlight to reme...
articles.body:
That's one way to close the halftime. The Philadelphia 76ers played the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night as VJ Edgecombe gave the Sixers a highlight to remember.

The young shooting guard drained a remarkable shot from beyond the half-court logo just before halftime against the Indiana Pacers. Edgecombe's deep three-pointer sent Philadelphia into the break with a 62-52 lead.

Edgecombe showed little hesitation as he launched the ball from well beyond the arc. The play provided a major highlight in a first half in which the 76ers built a 10-point advantage. Indiana struggled to find its rhythm, shooting just 39% from the field before the break.

However, the Pacers responded immediately after halftime. Indiana opened the third quarter with 17 unanswered points to take a 69-62 lead, turning a double-digit deficit into a seven-point advantage.

Philadelphia struggled to keep pace during the period, making just five of 21 shots from the field. Indiana, meanwhile, connected on 13 of its 23 attempts and carried an 88-75 lead into the fourth quarter.

The 76ers eventually rallied behind Tyrese Maxey, who finished with 27 points. His layup tied the game at 94, and two free throws put Philadelphia back in front with 5:15 remaining. Maxey later buried two three-pointers in the final 90 seconds to help secure a 114-109 victory.

Edgecombe, the third overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Baylor, continues to establish himself as a perimeter threat for Philadelphia. His buzzer-beater came just in time as one of the game's defining moments, even as the 76ers needed a fourth-quarter comeback to finish the job.

McAfee also praised Taylor as one of the league’s best running backs.“Yeah, this could be poker. But on that note, Jonathan Taylor is by far one of the best running backs in the league. There is no question about it,” Pat McAfee told Adam Schefter.Jonathan Taylor contract with Indianapolis ColtsJonathan Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August 2026. The deal includes a $15 million signing bonus, $39.02 million in guaranteed money, and a $22 million average annual income.In 2026, he is scheduled to earn a $6.98 million base salary, a $15 million signing bonus, and a $5,440 workout bonus, with a $16.19 million cap hit and $25.56 million in dead cap value. His total career earnings are $62 million over 7 NFL seasons, including 2026.Trading Taylor could be a significant financial decision for the franchise. His contract and production will attract contenders; however, interest alone doesn’t guarantee a deal.Indianapolis Colts owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon must deem the transaction fit. She may not want the Sauce Gardner mistake to be repeated. Still, if teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old running back, here are his landing spots.Jonathan Taylor landing spots include Denver and MinnesotaAccording to a report mentioned by NBC Sports’ Mike Florio, the Minnesota Vikings, Denver Broncos, Seattle Seahawks, and the Green Bay Packers have been linked to the Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.Pro Football Talk host Mike Florio thought the report mentioned the Packers as an odd choice because they got Josh Jacobs back. The analyst doesn’t think Green Bay will be trading for Taylor.It won’t be the Seahawks because they’ve already done business with them - Quenton Nelson. It could be the Vikings and the Broncos.Denver could be objectively looking at RJ Harvey and JK Dobbins, thinking, ’These guys are good, but they are not great.’ Jonathan Taylor could help push Denver’s offense where it needs to go. The passing game isn’t where it needs to be, and quarterback Bo Nix is still trying to find his footing.PFT Live co-host Chris Simms agrees with Mike Florio that the Broncos are the second-best landing spot for Jonathan Taylor. So, who’s it going to be? The Denver Broncos or the Minnesota Vikings.The Vikings seem to have their own show going with six straight wins. The Broncos might need a little push to go from good to great. So, would Ayanna Chapman’s worries come true? Only time will tell us that.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ideal Landing Spots for Top Available Skill Players at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away, and the market picked up on Tuesday when the Indianapolis Colts dealt guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away, and the market picked up on Tuesday when the Indianapolis Colts dealt guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

While Nelson and Buckner are exactly the sort of foundational difference-makers that teams with Super Bowl aspirations should be chasing, many fans are waiting to see if Indianapolis will part with star running back Jonathan Taylor.

Of course, there's no guarantee that the Colts will part with the face of their offense. Fortunately for teams in need of additional offensive potency, he isn't the only option likely to be available.

Here, we'll run down 10 skill players who could be available ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and the top landing spot for each. All analysis is based on past production, contract status, team trajectory, team needs, and any relevant recent rumors.

Players are listed in alphabetical order.

The Arizona Cardinals have already moved one notable player, sending receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. At 2-5, the Cardinals are unlikely to contend in the brutal NFC West, and if they decide to keep trading players, Tyler Allgeier would be a logical candidate.

Arizona signed Allgeier to a two-year, $12.3 million deal this offseason but quickly made him a backup behind talented rookie Jeremiyah Love . With Love out the last two weeks, Allgeier has also been outperformed by Zonovan Knight.

The Cardinals couldn't expect more than a mid-Day 3 pick in return for Allgeier, but they would save $1.6 million in 2026 cap space and $5.2 million in 2027 cap room.

If Allgeier is available, the Detroit Lions would be a terrific spot for him. Allgeier has averaged just 2.9 yards per carry this year, but he has averaged a solid 4.1 yards per carry over the course of his career.

At 5'10" and 225 pounds, Allgeier is also a bigger back who could complement Jahmyr Gibbs in the same way David Montgomery once did. Gibbs has fared well as a high-volume back for Detroit this season, but he's on pace for a whopping 470 touches.

Adding someone to help share the load down the stretch would make plenty of sense for the Lions.

The Colts appear to have begun a fire sale, and the Philadelphia Eagles are a team that could soon follow suit. The Eagles have been ravaged by injuries and are highly unlikely to have starting quarterback Jalen Hurts in the lineup again before 2027.

At 2-5, the Eagles aren't entirely out of the NFC East race, but they're certainly trending in the wrong direction.

GM Howie Roseman has already traded center Cam Jurgens, and if he continues selling off pieces, Marquise Brown would be a logical trade chip. Philly signed him to a one-year, $5 million deal this offseason but has barely put him on the field.

Brown has appeared in two games and caught his first two passes of the season on Monday night. The Eagles couldn't expect more than a late-round pick for him, but he's clearly expendable, even with multiple injuries at receiver.

If Brown is moved, the Kansas City Chiefs would be the most logical destination. Kansas City could use more receiver depth, and the 29-year-old spent his last two seasons with the Chiefs.

Last season, Brown caught 49 passes for 587 yards and five touchdowns in Kansas City.

Taylor isn't the only Colts skill player who could be moved before November 10. If wide receiver Josh Downs gets his way, he'll be playing elsewhere for the second half of the season.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Downs has requested a trade.

Moving Downs would make some sense for Indianapolis, as the 25-year-old is in the final year of his contract. With 26 catches and 307 yards on his 2026 resume, He would probably bring something in the range of a high Day 3 pick from a receiver-needy team.

In 54 career games, Downs has caught 224 passes for 2,447 yards and 11 touchdowns.

Downs' route-running and change-of-direction skills would fit well with the Pittsburgh Steelers' precision-passing offense. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't regularly stretched the field this season and has instead looked to beat defenses with decision-making and high-percentage throws.

Rodgers could use a target like Downs, especially with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson on injured reserve. Plus, Steelers general manager Omar Khan already has an Indianapolis pipeline open after acquiring Pittman in an offseason trade.

Tight end Dallas Goedert is another sensible trade chip if the Eagles decide to punt on the 2026 season, though he's anything but if Philly believes it can still contend.

With DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and Saquon Barkley all injured, Goedert is the most reliable skill player the Eagles have right now. He had five catches for 48 yards on Monday night and has 228 yards on the season.

Goedert is also 31 years old, though, and is playing on a one-year, $7 million deal. Trading him now would make sense if Roseman is ready to pack it in for the year. He'd probably net a high Day 3 selection in a trade.

The Chicago Bears would be a terrific landing spot for Goedert, though that wouldn't have been the case a week ago. Chicago has a terrific pass-catching tight end in Colston Loveland and a great second option in Cole Kmet.

The problem for Chicago is that Kmet suffered a knee injury in Week 7 and was subsequently placed on season-ending injured reserve.

Ben Johnson has regularly used formations that feature two or three tight ends this season, and while Kmet wasn't a focal point of the passing attack, he was a great ancillary target who provided offensive flexibility. Goedert would be a great replacement for the remainder of the season.

The Minnesota Vikings signed wide receiver Jauan Jennings to a one-year, $8 million contract this offseason. However, he hasn't quite been the high-floor third receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison that the Vikings hoped he could be.

Jennings has just four catches for 43 yards in five appearances this year.

This is why the Vikings could consider moving Jennings, even as they sit as the league's last undefeated team. Minnesota could also save $5 million in cap space.

The Vikings probably couldn't get more than a fifth- or sixth-round pick for Jennings, but any draft capital and cap flexibility they gain could be used to address areas of greater need—like running back. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, though, Minnesota isn't actively shopping the 29-year-old.

However, Schefter told The Pat McAfee Show (beginning at the 1:35:10 mark) that while no trade is imminent, teams have "checked in" on Jennings.

If Jennings is on the move, a return to the San Francisco 49ers would be the ideal outcome. San Francisco needs receiver help with Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans both injured, and Jennings logged 643 yards and nine touchdowns with the 49ers last season.

The Cleveland Browns are a surprising 5-2, but they're not good enough to sell off important contributors and still expect to make a playoff run.

This is why veteran Jerry Jeudy isn't being actively shopped, according to Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

"The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high," they noted. "It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on—even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal."

While Jeudy won't be available for cheap, a strong offer might get a deal done. Rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are the future at receiver for Cleveland. Trading Jeudy would save $3.9 million in 2026 cap space and $7 million in 2027.

A strong offer would likely mean at least a conditional fourth-round pick—a higher-round selection than the 2024 fifth- and sixth-round picks Cleveland sent the Denver Broncos to acquire Jeudy more than two years ago. A team surrendering that pick would have to value the 27-year-old in both the short and long term.

The Los Angeles Rams, who already swung one trade with Cleveland this year to land Myles Garrett, would be such a team.

Los Angeles is trying to chase a Super Bowl in 2026 but won't have No. 2 receiver Davante Adams for the foreseeable future because of a hamstring injury . It may also want to replace the 33-year-old Adams with a younger receiver after this season.

While Jeudy's drop issues are concerning, his precision route-running and breakaway ability would mesh perfectly with Sean McVay's spacing-based offense.

Quentin Johnston, WR, Los Angeles Chargers

According to Schefter and Rapoport , the Los Angeles Chargers "insist they are trying to win games" and have given "no indication" that they're looking to be sellers at the trade deadline. However, Los Angeles' stance doesn't change the fact that it is the only winless team left in the NFL this season.

Even if the Chargers were clinging to playoff hopes, moving fourth-year receiver Quentin Johnston would make some level of sense. The 2023 first-round pick showed some flashes of promise over the last two seasons but has again disappeared in the offense this year.

Through five appearances, Johnston has just eight catches for 165 yards.

While Los Angeles did exercise the fifth-year option on Johnston's rookie contract, it's hard to envision him sticking with the club long-term. Getting a fourth- or fifth-round pick for the 25-year-old now would be sensible.

The New York Giants could provide Johnston with a great landing spot if he is on the move. New York is pushing for a playoff spot, has an intriguing collection of young offensive playmakers, and could use another dynamic receiver to complement Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields this season and beyond.

The Giants also happen to employ offensive coordinator Greg Roman, who was the Chargers' OC when Johnston topped 700 receiving yards in both 2024 and 2025.

Ideal Landing Spot: Washington Commanders

The Tennessee Titans have looked like a fairly functional football team over the past two weeks, and running back Tony Pollard has been a huge part of the equation. He recorded 76 scrimmage yards in the Week 6 win over Indy, and he logged 155 yards and three touchdowns in a close loss to Cleveland last week.

However, the fact remains that Tennessee is 1-6, and Pollard probably won't be with the franchise much longer. He's in the final year of his contract, and he'll turn 30 in April. Moving him now would probably net the Titans a fourth- or fifth-round pick.

At that price point, Pollard would make a ton of sense for the Washington Commanders. At 1-4-1, Washington is sitting in the NFC East basement, but it has a healthier overall roster than Philadelphia's.

The Commanders rank ninth in rushing yards and 10th in yards per carry. However, those numbers are a bit misleading, as quarterback Jayden Daniels has regularly chewed up yards on the ground.

Lead running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has averaged just 3.6 yards per carry this season. The Commanders added Austin Ekeler in an effort to boost their ground game.

Adding Pollard would help boost Washington's backfield in a big way and would give the Commanders another playmaker as they try to offset the loss of wide receiver Terry McLaurin.

Taylor is a massive potential trade target because he's an elite running back and one of the top offensive difference-makers in the league. Through seven games this season, he has logged 765 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns.

While Downs has reportedly requested a trade, Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Wednesday that Taylor has not. According to Schefter, Indianapolis doesn't want to move Taylor either.

Schefter told The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday (beginning at the 1:24:18 mark) that his "understanding" is that Colts ownership doesn't want to trade its star running back.

Indianapolis appears open for business, and the right offer could still pry Taylor away from the Colts. According to ESPN's Jordan Raanan , Taylor would cost a second-round draft pick and "possibly more."

If Taylor can be had, the Vikings would be the best spot for him. They have a championship-caliber defense, a couple of great wide receivers, and a head coach in Kevin O'Connell who could maximize Taylor's rushing and receiving ability.

Minnesota also has some questions at running back, as Aaron Jones continues to battle an MCL sprain.

Adding Taylor could help spark Minnesota's 29th-ranked offense as O'Connell tries to coax better play out of quarterback Kyler Murray. If successful, that might be enough to push the Vikings deep into the postseason.

Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. recorded 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie Pro Bowler in 2024. Instead of trending upward since then, however, he's gone in the opposite direction.

This season, Thomas has just nine catches for 105 yards and one score. He didn't see the field in the second half of Jacksonville's last game.

While the Jags have publicly tried to hype Thomas as an important piece of the offense, it's becoming clear that he simply isn't under head coach Liam Coen. Some around the league believe a trade is inevitable.

"There are a lot of people around the league who believe Thomas could have a new home by the trade deadline," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote last week.

Expect Thomas to command a package similar to the second- and sixth-round picks the Cardinals got for Harrison.

While contenders like Kansas City and Pittsburgh could use a big-play threat like Thomas, his best home might be with a rebuilding team that has upside. It could take some time for him to regain his rookie form, and a Super Bowl hopeful might not be able to afford him that.

The Las Vegas Raiders, however, could. They have yet to turn the page from quarterback Kirk Cousins to rookie first overall pick Fernando Mendoza . There's a chance they won't hand Mendoza the keys until next season.

As a potential long-term contributor, Thomas would be a great fit in Klint Kubiak's offense alongside Mendoza, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and possibly Tre Tucker, who will be a free agent in the spring.

articles.summary: It's now or never. If you're going to salvage your season—or gear up for a championship push—it has to happen now. With injuries piling up and the bye weeks causing stress, you better swing for the fences now.
articles.body:
It's now or never. If you're going to salvage your season—or gear up for a championship push—it has to happen now. With injuries piling up and the bye weeks causing stress, you better swing for the fences now.

As always, the weekly fantasy football trade value chart is here to provide an assist.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a descending trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

With the Indianapolis Colts in fire sale mode, Jonathan Taylor's status from a fantasy football perspective becomes one of the more fascinating topics when it comes to potential trade targets.

Is he going to get traded? Would moving to a different team increase his value or actually be a downgrade? If he stays in Indianapolis, how detrimental will the loss of Quenton Nelson be to his fantasy value? How quickly would the tanking Colts consider shutting him down if he deals with even the most minor of injures?

You need to be monitoring this situation carefully. If the Colts are selling top players, which they've already started doing, a Taylor relocation would probably be best for him from a fantasy perspective. If he lands on a top offense, his fantasy ceiling is absolutely elite.

As it stands, he remains highly valuable and you shouldn't panic sell and take a bad deal. But it wouldn't be a bad idea to gauge whether there's interest in him around your league either.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 8 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: Sometimes, the early bettor gets the favorable spread, as Bleacher Report's expert crew did when they jumped on a couple of lines in Week 8.
articles.body:
Sometimes, the early bettor gets the favorable spread, as Bleacher Report's expert crew did when they jumped on a couple of lines in Week 8.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , initially made their picks amid speculation about Saquon Barkley's injury status and before Indianapolis traded two key veterans. O'Donnell subsequently switched his selection from the Colts to the Jaguars.

Oddsmakers have shifted the lines for the Eagles' and Colts' games over the last 24 hours.

Coming off their best week of the season, our experts feel confident about this week's picks. Can they keep it going in Week 8?

Before we dive into the upcoming slate, check out the panel's standings against the spread through seven weeks.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Public betting trend information is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Carolina Panthers (3-3) at Green Bay Packers (4-3)

In short-rest Thursday night games this season, the home teams are 4-2 against the spread. The Packers have won each of their last two home games by double digits and should be motivated back at Lambeau after a close road loss to Detroit. Look for Josh Jacobs to get rolling against a toothless defense that was annihilated on the ground last week.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers bludgeoned the Panthers during last weekend's meeting between the division rivals. Carolina couldn't stop the run. That's OK, because the Packers can't run the ball. When the league's worst run defense faces its bottom-ranked ground game, this meeting becomes the movable object versus the stoppable force. However, Carolina should hold an advantage against the Packers' offensive line since the latter is also one of the worst units in pass-block win rate .

Panthers: Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (1-6) at Cincinnati Bengals (4-2)

Spreads this size are always tricky, and the Titans have shown a pulse the last two times out, beating the Colts outright and giving the 5-2 Browns all they could handle. But Tennessee is also a one-win team that ranks last in the NFL in total offense and 31st in points scored.

The Bengals just dropped a 35-0 half on the Ravens at Paycor Stadium. Cincinnati's pass rush and explosive passing game make a double-digit win a strong possibility.

Five of Tennessee's seven games have been decided by six points or fewer. In their only other game this season as double-digit underdogs, they went to Baltimore and covered in a six-point loss. The oddsmakers want you to buy the Bengals high here, but I don't trust them yet. Throw in the backdoor cover potential and the Titans are the obvious choice.

Bengals: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Baltimore Ravens (4-3) at Buffalo Bills (5-1)

I think the Bills likely win this game on extra rest, but I don't love the hook. This veteran Ravens team is extremely unlikely to go down easily after being embarrassed in the second half against Cincinnati in Week 7.

This changes if Lamar Jackson doesn't play again, but the last two games between Baltimore and Buffalo were decided by a total of three points and I'm expecting something similar if Jackson suits up in Orchard Park Sunday.

I don't know what version of Lamar Jackson we'll see if he gets onto the field this week. These two AFC contenders, when healthy, could play 100 times and split it 50-50.

The hook is definitely the biggest concern in what should be a close game, but my gut says that even if this one goes to the final possession, it'll take more than a field goal to decide the outcome.

I'm content leaning on Josh Allen at home with the Bills' defense likely to make a surprisingly big play when the game matters.

Bills: Hanford , Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals (2-5) at Dallas Cowboys (3-4)

The Cowboys come off a big divisional win over the Eagles on Monday and face a Cardinals team that allows more points than any team in the league. That could be the recipe for another lopsided win for Dallas, but I don't trust the Cowboys' defense to turn in two strong performances in a row. The Cowboys will win and control most of this game, but Jacoby Brissett throws a late touchdown to force a backdoor cover.

If Dallas wants to be taken seriously as a playoff-caliber team, it needs dominant back-to-back wins against non-playoff clubs. The Cowboys are on a short week, and the Cardinals upset the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago, but after finding their rhythm last Monday, Dak Prescott and his playmakers should be able to flex their muscle at home against a lesser opponent despite the Cardinals' 4-0 record at AT&T Stadium .

Cardinals: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Sobleski

Cleveland Browns (5-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2)

The Steelers narrowly lost to the Browns a few weeks ago, but that was in Cleveland, on a short week, and before Pittsburgh started to find a bit of offensive rhythm.

The Steelers' offense actually came to life late in that one, though it proved to be too late to prevent the Browns from engineering one of the game-winning drives that have become their 2026 trademark.

While the Browns have been fun, they've also been significantly slow starters this season, and I think that'll offset any jet lag the Steelers experience after last week's international game. Now that Pittsburgh has figured out how to get Rico Dowdle and Germie Bernard involved in its offense, the Browns may fall into an early hole that is too big to escape.

Cleveland hasn't won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003. While that's a trend that will eventually be bucked, I don't think this year's Browns squad will be the one to do it.

At this point, there's no reason to bet against the Browns, because they continually find a way. Granted, it's never pretty. But this team has a formula that works by letting its defense dictate most of the game then allowing the offense to make plays late in the contest to sneak away with another victory.

With the point spread factored in and Cleveland having already shown this exact approach worked against the Steelers, the Browns get the nod.

Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton

Indianapolis Colts (2-5) at Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2)

I initially picked the Colts before they traded away important starters on both sides of the ball. The trades, both completely understandable from a big-picture perspective given where Indy's season is going, could be a catalyst for an inspired performance from the road team.

The hook is also a cause for concern, but it's not enough to buy into the Jaguars laying an egg off their bye week. Jacksonville has the league's best run defense and will not let Jonathan Taylor beat them.

No, this one could get ugly if Liam Coen wants it to.

The Indianapolis Colts have begun selling ahead of the trade deadline, moving Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

The next major question is whether Indianapolis will also move Jonathan Taylor as it reshapes its roster.

How much the two-time NFL rushing touchdown leader actually plays in the coming weeks will be fascinating to watch as Indianapolis' front office navigates his potential departure. As a result, Indianapolis is no longer in a position to compete, especially against the AFC South's best team, who happens to be coming off a bye.

Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Minnesota Vikings (6-0) at Detroit Lions (4-2)

Don't let the Vikings' undefeated record fool you. They're good but not dominant. Minnesota beat the Miami Dolphins 15-10 in Week 4 and just squeaked by the Indianapolis Colts 16-10 last week.

Kyler Murray has been inconsistent in five outings, throwing for three touchdowns and two interceptions while averaging 162.4 passing yards per game. He won't keep pace with the Lions' second-ranked scoring offense, even if Detroit scores only 21-24 points.

At worst, this is another push against the spread in a divisional matchup for the Lions.

The Vikings may be one of the ugliest all-around 6-0 teams we've seen; averaging just over 20 points per game in today's NFL is rarely a blueprint for success. The defense, though, holds opponents to a meager 12.3 points per game, and Minnesota leads the league in turnover differential.

Jared Goff has yet to throw an interception this season for a Lions team that ranks behind only the Bills in points per game. Something is going to break in this one, or it'll be ugly, and I'm taking the points, leaning defense over offense.

Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Atlanta Falcons (3-4) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5)

In more than a few ways, these teams are mirror images of one another. Both the Falcons and Buccaneers rely heavily on the run game offensively. Both teams have underrated defenses that aren't easy to run the ball against—neither squad is allowing 90 yards a game on the ground. That leaves it to the passing games to determine who gets the victory here, so go with the team that threw for more than 64 yards in Week 7.

Both the Falcons and Buccaneers have stellar run defenses, so this game may come down to which QB plays better. The Bucs beat the Panthers in Baker Mayfield's return to the field, but that was more about leaning on the run game than Mayfield steering the ship. Michael Penix Jr. has six touchdowns in his last two starts, including three in the Falcons' Week 7 upset win over the 49ers. I think Atlanta will carry that momentum and earn a big NFC South win here.

Falcons: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) at New York Jets (2-5)

Both of these teams are desperate for a win. The Jets have lost five of their last six games, and the Raiders have lost four straight. In these circumstances, you typically favor the home team.

The Jets also have more offensive firepower than the Raiders. Rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. has posted back-to-back 103-plus-yard receiving games, with touchdowns in both. Second-year tight end Mason Taylor caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns last week. Garrett Wilson should see more targets after letting out some frustrations . Running back Breece Hall could return from a quad injury and join Braelon Allen in threatening the Raiders' 30th-ranked run defense.

Las Vegas has All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, and wideout Tre Tucker is starting to show he can be a lead receiver, but that's about it. The Raiders' run game is nonexistent, with the second-fewest yards per contest, and their defense has allowed 27-plus points in five straight games.

The Jets have the stronger collection of offensive playmakers, though game management could be decisive in a matchup this close.

The Raiders are barreling toward the Fernando Mendoza era as they ride this four-game losing streak. That losing streak is courtesy of the Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The Jets are not those teams.

This game could go either way as both teams fight to keep their seasons remotely relevant, but I'll buy into the Raiders for one more game before things really go off the rails with the 49ers, Seahawks, and Broncos on their schedule over the next three weeks.

Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) at Los Angeles Rams (3-4)

I don't think the Chargers get their first win here, but I do think they keep it close as they come in rested off their bye week.

I keep waiting to see the dominant Rams team that everyone expected to see this season, but I'm not sure when or if we're going to get it as they deal with injuries and an inconsistent offense.

I don't see Justin Herbert coming in and suddenly looking like his old self, but the Chargers can make this one ugly enough to keep it within a touchdown in the end.

This is more points than I'd prefer to lay with a Rams team that has been oddly inconsistent this season. That's especially true against a Chargers team that is coming off its bye and has far more talent on its roster than its 0-6 record would suggest.

With both teams sharing SoFi Stadium, the Rams may have little home-field advantage. Meanwhile, injuries continue to mount for Sean McVay's team.

Yet, we finally saw a good all-around performance from the Rams in Week 7. I think we'll see another strong effort from McVay's squad this week as the Rams fight to prove, possibly to themselves, that they are more than just good.

Chargers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) at Denver Broncos (5-2)

Laying points on the road with a team coming off a lopsided loss is risky—especially when Denver recently beat the Seattle team responsible for that defeat.

Both the Chiefs and Broncos are stout defensively and have questions on offense—and Denver's concerns have grown with Jaylen Waddle potentially missing this contest.

This has the makings of a close, low-scoring game. If that's the case, give this writer Patrick Mahomes over Bo Nix.

We finally saw an offensive outburst from the Denver Broncos in Week 7. While I do believe that was largely the product of playing a lackluster Arizona Cardinals defense, I think the Broncos will be able to replicate at least some of that success against Kansas City.

Meanwhile, I don't think the Chiefs' offense will be able to do what it did to the Broncos at home in Week 1.

Kenneth Walker III will give the Chiefs a chance to exploit Denver's 28th-ranked run defense. However, I think the Broncos' defense can limit him enough and force enough mistakes to even the series with a close win in Denver.

Chiefs: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

New England Patriots (4-3) at Miami Dolphins (1-5)

The Dolphins finally got their first win and are home, but the Patriots will be rested after a Thursday night road loss to the Bears. Miami has been more competitive than I expected this season, despite only having one win, but this feels like a get-right spot for Drake Maye and the New England offense. I think the Patriots win by double digits.

The Dolphins feel good after beating the New York Jets, their first win of the season, but they'll face a much better opponent in the Patriots, who had extra time to prepare after last Thursday's loss to the Bears. Moreover, the Dolphins' seventh-ranked rushing attack won't be able to run over the Patriots' eighth-ranked run defense as it did against the Jets last week.

This is a good spot for Drake Maye and A.J. Brown to get in sync in a lopsided victory. Miami ranks 19th in passing yards allowed and has surrendered 14 passing touchdowns in six games.

Patriots: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) at Washington Commanders (1-4-1)

I know the Eagles are a mess, but they held a second-half lead over Dallas on Monday night. Let's not overrate a Washington team that has one victory all season and hasn't won a home game by more than a field goal since last September.

Washington had two weeks to prepare for an Eagles squad without Jalen Hurts in the lineup and a clearly hampered Saquon Barkley due to a lingering hamstring injury. Washington made some horrific mental mistakes during its previous two games, though.

While those were unacceptable at the time, the team had to spend the extra time getting everyone on the same page and rallying for the second half of the season. It's now time to get going against a depleted opponent. Otherwise, it won't happen this season.

Eagles: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell

Chicago Bears (5-2) at Seattle Seahawks (4-3)

I'd like this pick exponentially more with the hook, but even without it I'm taking the points. Seattle's defense was lights-out last week against the Chiefs under the lights at Lumen Field, and the last time the Bears faced a stiff road test they got boatraced at Lambeau.

But Chicago's offense is playing at an entirely different level than Kansas City's, and the Bears' defense has been opportunistic.

A late Sam Darnold turnover could give Chicago the opening it needs to win with a field goal.

The Bears have a lot going for them entering this matchup.

They're coming off their mini-bye after playing last Thursday night, and they have an offense that has topped 30 points in every full game it has played with Caleb Williams this season. They also have a defense that has become very adept at forcing turnovers and getting off the field on third downs.

However, Chicago hasn't faced a defense as good as Seattle's since, perhaps, its Week 2 clash with the Minnesota Vikings—the game in which Williams was injured.

The Seahawks' offense has been very inconsistent, but I'm still not entirely sold on Chicago's defense. It has its strengths and ranks top 10 in points allowed, but it also ranks 23rd in yards per carry allowed and 31st in net yards per pass attempt allowed. I'm very interested to see how the Bears respond to a low-scoring, grind-it-out game, which is what I believe we'll see here.

I'm much more confident in Seattle's ability to win such a game at home.

Bears: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 8 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: It's a tough week for fantasy football managers without Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans, both of whom are dealing with injuries and are on bye. Managers with Malik Nabers, Cam Skattebo, Isaiah Likely, Chris Olave, C.J. Stroud or Nico Collins will also need replacements, as all six are on bye.
articles.body:
It's a tough week for fantasy football managers without Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans, both of whom are dealing with injuries and are on bye. Managers with Malik Nabers, Cam Skattebo, Isaiah Likely, Chris Olave, C.J. Stroud or Nico Collins will also need replacements, as all six are on bye.

That said, our Week 8 sleepers highlight viable fill-ins for the fantasy stars missing in your lineups at a pivotal time in the season.

The quarterback selections are journeymen with top-eight matchups. Pickings are slim at running back, but a rookie has emerged in a sizeable role within a committee and has flex appeal.

As usual, injuries are shifting NFL depth charts, and two No. 2 wide receivers will see more targets as attrition takes its toll. Lastly, keep tabs on a couple of tight ends in pass-friendly games with decent over/under totals.

Here are our top sleepers at every position—all available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros ' consensus percentages.

QB Jacoby Brissett at Dallas Cowboys (23 Percent Rostered)

Jacoby Brissett has finished within the top seven in fantasy scoring in two of seven weeks. Now, he has a favorable matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, who are tied for eighth in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

After throwing for at least two touchdowns in three straight games between Weeks 3 and 5, Brissett posted modest stat lines in tough matchups with the Los Angeles Rams, who allow the fourth-fewest passing yards per game, and the Denver Broncos, who allow the sixth-fewest touchdown passes per contest.

Brissett should be able to move the ball against the Cowboys' generous pass coverage. Dallas allowed only one touchdown pass apiece to Jalon Daniels, Jordan Love and Tanner McKee, but those numbers need context: Daniels was making his second career start, Love's receivers dropped multiple passes in the end zone, and McKee was making only his second start of the season.

As a more experienced starting signal-caller with All-Pro tight end Trey McBride at his disposal, Brissett should be able to put points on the board with his arm.

QB Geno Smith vs. Las Vegas Raiders (21 Percent Rostered)

Geno Smith may have this game circled on his calendar. He has a favorable matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, who traded him to the New York Jets this past offseason.

The 36-year-old had a rough 2025 campaign in Las Vegas, both on the field and with fans , amid a frustrating season.

Smith has already thrown three touchdown passes apiece against the Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins, who have allowed the most and seventh-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, respectively. The Raiders have allowed the fifth-most.

With star wide receiver Garrett Wilson, emerging rookie first-round wideout Omar Cooper Jr., and budding second-year tight end Mason Taylor, Smith has the playmakers to post a strong stat line against the Raiders' 22nd-ranked pass defense.

Las Vegas has allowed an average of three touchdown passes over the last five weeks, giving up multiple touchdowns through the air in each game.

RB Jonah Coleman vs. Kansas City Chiefs (40 Percent Rostered)

It's rare for a team's No. 3 running back in a committee to have standalone fantasy value, but the Denver Broncos have roles for their trio of tailbacks. J.K. Dobbins is the primary early-down ball-carrier. RJ Harvey has the primary pass-catching role. Coleman can play on all three downs, and he's logged 11 and 13 touches in his last two outings.

Coleman has big-play ability, averaging 4.9 yards per carry, with five catches for 34 yards, including two first-down receptions. He missed four games with a high ankle sprain, but head coach Sean Payton believes the rookie fourth-rounder has earned his touches .

While it's practical to avoid a muddled backfield, Coleman's efficiency makes him a sleeper flex option. He has 24 touches for 127 yards and a touchdown.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , wideout Jaylen Waddle's availability for this game is uncertain after he aggravated a chest injury last Sunday. Without him, the Broncos may rely on their running backs on the ground and in the short passing game, which means enough touches to go around for their backfield platoon.

Keep in mind that the Kansas City Chiefs allowed Seattle Seahawks running backs to rack up 146 scrimmage yards and a touchdown last week.

RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. Indianapolis Colts (19 Percent Rostered)

The Indianapolis Colts have pivoted their focus toward the future, trading three-time first-team All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and three-time Pro Bowler DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Colts wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade. So, Indianapolis may keep him inactive or limit his snaps while it weighs trade proposals from potential suitors.

The Colts' season is going off the rails, and that could impact their play on the field. If the Jacksonville Jaguars jump out to a significant early lead, they can hand off to their top two running backs and cruise for most of the game.

With the Jaguars' potentially run-heavy game script, Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. could get enough work on the ground to produce fantasy-friendly stat lines.

Rodriguez won't offer much in the short passing game (one catch for six yards this season), but he's logged at least six carries in five of six outings and finished Week 6 with 11 touches.

The Jaguars also get a favorable matchup for their ground attack, facing a defense that's tied for 12th in fantasy points allowed to running backs and allows 4.8 yards per carry, 28th in the league. It's worth noting that Rodriguez has handled 10 of 26 red-zone carries , totaling 25 yards and a touchdown this season.

WR Antonio Williams vs. Philadelphia Eagles (12 Percent Rostered)

The Washington Commanders placed Terry McLaurin on season-ending injured reserve with a torn patellar tendon. As a result, rookie third-rounder Antonio Williams will likely see more targets.

Williams is ready for an expanded role. He has at least three receptions in five out of six games. The Commanders have split his snaps between the perimeter and the slot, so he's interchangeable with lead wideout Stefon Diggs, who's also versatile.

Last Monday, the Philadelphia Eagles gave up three passing touchdowns and allowed three Dallas Cowboys receivers to rack up at least 57 receiving yards. This isn't the same Eagles defense that allowed the eighth-fewest passing yards last year; the unit ranks 26th in that category through seven games.

As the No. 2 wide receiver, Williams could outshine fellow rookie wideout Makai Lemon in the Sunday Night Football showcase.

WR Kendrick Bourne at Dallas Cowboys (8 Percent Rostered)

The Arizona Cardinals are thin at wide receiver. Two weeks ago, they traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. Last week, fourth-year wideout Jalen Brooks suffered a season-ending wrist injury.

Michael Wilson is the Cardinals' No. 1 receiver, but he has finished with no more than four catches and 55 receiving yards in each of his last three games.

Kendrick Bourne has seen at least six targets in each of the previous three games. In Arizona's outing against the Detroit Lions' 32nd-ranked pass defense, he caught five passes for 70 yards.

This week, Bourne draws a plus matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, who allow the sixth-most fantasy points to wide receivers.

If the Cowboys' top cornerback, Joey Porter Jr., lines up against Wilson, Bourne could have a big day alongside All-Pro tight end Trey McBride in the passing game.

TE Cade Otton vs. Atlanta Falcons (8 Percent Rostered)

Yes, it's true: Cade Otton finished with a goose egg in his box score last week, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't need to throw the ball because they dominated the Carolina Panthers on the ground, rushing for 258 yards and three touchdowns. Baker Mayfield only threw 11 passes, completing seven for 64 yards and a touchdown.

The Buccaneers won't run through the Atlanta Falcons' fourth-ranked run defense. Mayfield will have to play a bigger role in his team's offensive success, and he could target Cade Otton several times.

The Falcons' 29th-ranked pass defense has been vulnerable to big-bodied pass-catchers, ranking 10th in fantasy points allowed to tight ends. In four straight weeks, Atlanta has allowed opposing tight end groups to accumulate at least 54 receiving yards.

Otton is the only tight end with notable production in the Buccaneers' aerial attack. He ranks third on the team in targets (30), receptions (19) and receiving yards (186). Otton isn't an athletic playmaker, but he's worth consideration with FanDuel's over/under total set at 44.5 for this game. With two top-four run defenses on the field, expect the passing attacks to rack up yards and points.

TE Mason Taylor vs. Las Vegas Raiders (3 Percent Rostered)

Rookie first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq generated buzz with his breakout performance against the Detroit Lions, hauling in seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, but second-year tight end Mason Taylor has made his presence felt in the passing game, catching 14 passes for 117 yards and two touchdowns.

Taylor is coming off his first two-touchdown outing and could continue to play a bigger role than Sadiq in the Jets' offense.

The 22-year-old has played 57 percent of the offensive snaps and has seen six targets in back-to-back games, while Sadiq has seen four total targets in less than 38 percent of the snaps over the last two weeks.

Smith's developing rapport with Taylor puts him on the radar as a solid TE2 with a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, who allow the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends.

Last week, the Raiders gave up two touchdowns to Davis Allen, the Los Angeles Rams' third-string tight end.

articles.title: Here are 5 things to know about NFL Week 8
articles.summary: The NFL season is approaching its midway point, and the stakes are getting higher.
articles.body: The NFL season is approaching its midway point, and the stakes are getting higher. From a marquee showdown between two of the AFC’s biggest stars to the league’s last unbeaten team facing its toughest test yet, here are five things to know heading into Week 8. Josh Allen vs. Lamar Jackson The marquee matchup Sunday features Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, fresh off their bye week, hosting Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens. Jackson is expected to return from an ankle injury, and the Ravens desperately need their two-time MVP back on the field after last week’s stunning collapse against the Cincinnati Bengals. Baltimore became just the third team in NFL history to lose by at least 20 points after leading by 13 or more at halftime. Jackson is 3-2 all-time against Allen in the regular season but has lost both of their playoff meetings. While both teams have Super Bowl aspirations, the stakes are considerably higher for Baltimore. At 4-3, the Ravens suddenly find themselves in last place in what has become a surprisingly competitive AFC North. The 5-1 Bills, meanwhile, sit comfortably atop the AFC East. Browns-Steelers: First place on the line Speaking of the AFC North, how about those first-place Cleveland Browns? Not many people expected Cleveland to be sitting at 5-2 heading into Week 8, but the Browns have found a way to win close games, thanks in large part to Deshaun Watson’s late-game heroics. Watson has engineered a game-winning drive in all five of Cleveland’s victories this season. He’s the only quarterback with five game-winning drives this year and just the third in NFL history to accomplish that feat in his team’s first five wins of a season, joining Troy Aikman in 1990 and Matthew Stafford in 2016. Now comes another major test. The Browns head to Pittsburgh to face the 5-2 Steelers, who are coming off a long but happy flight home from Paris after beating the New Orleans Saints 16-10 last Sunday. This is the second meeting between these division rivals this season, with Cleveland winning a 27-24 thriller in Week 4. Can Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers get their revenge? One thing is certain: Somebody is leaving Sunday at 6-2 and sitting alone atop the AFC North (unless, of course, there’s a tie). Perfect Vikings: How long can Minnesota keep this up? And then there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, sitting at a perfect 6-0. But a closer look at their numbers reveals one of the more unusual unbeaten starts in recent memory. If you looked strictly at Minnesota’s offensive statistics, you’d probably guess this was a .500 team at best. The Vikings rank 28th in total offense and 23rd in scoring. So how are they undefeated? Two words: Brian Flores. Minnesota’s blitz-happy defensive coordinator has put together the most dominant unit in football. The Vikings are allowing just 12 points per game, easily the best mark in the NFL. The next-closest defenses, Kansas City and Jacksonville, are surrendering 17 points per game. That’s an incredible gap, but it also raises a legitimate question: How long can Minnesota keep winning without much help from its offense? We’ll get a better idea over the next four weeks, which will be their toughest stretch of the season. On Sunday, the Vikings travel to Detroit to face a dangerous Lions offense before taking on the Bills, Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers. If Minnesota wants to keep its perfect season alive, Kyler Murray and the offense will likely have to do more than simply stay out of the defense’s way. Battle of Los Angeles: Not exactly what we expected Back in September, a Week 8 showdown between the Rams and Chargers looked like it could be one of the most entertaining games on the NFL schedule. Fast-forward to October and this matchup has lost much of its luster. The Rams finally snapped their two-game losing streak with a win over the Las Vegas Raiders, but at 3-4, they are still searching for the form that made them the preseason Super Bowl favorites. Things are considerably worse for their Los Angeles neighbors. The Chargers are the NFL’s only remaining winless team, stumbling to an 0-6 start for the first time since 2000. Despite that disastrous beginning, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers made no sweeping changes during their bye week, although Harbaugh said nothing was off the table as the team searches for answers. At this point, the Chargers are playing for pride. The Rams, however, still have plenty to play for. With the 49ers and Seattle Seahawks setting the pace in the NFC West, Los Angeles can ill afford another setback. A loss to the winless Chargers would drop the Rams to 3-5 and leave their once-promising season in serious jeopardy. For a team that entered the season with championship expectations, this has suddenly become a must-win game. NFC Championship preview? For the second straight week, the defending Super Bowl champions find themselves in a massive prime-time showdown. And this one could very well be a preview of the NFC Championship Game. The Seahawks host the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football, fresh off a dominant 20-3 victory over the Chiefs on Sunday night. Seattle’s defense was nothing short of spectacular, holding Kansas City to its fewest points, total yards and first downs in any game started by Patrick Mahomes. Now, Mike Macdonald’s defense faces a completely different challenge: trying to slow down arguably the most entertaining offense in football. Ben Johnson has transformed the Bears into an offensive juggernaut, with Caleb Williams leading an attack capable of putting up points in bunches. In the three games Williams has started and finished, Chicago has scored 59, 31 and 30 points. But lighting up the scoreboard against Seattle is an entirely different proposition. Full Week 8 schedule Thursday Carolina Panthers @ Green Bay Packers, 8:15 p.m. ET Sunday Arizona Cardinals @ Dallas Cowboys, 1 p.m. ET Indianapolis Colts @ Jacksonville Jaguars, 1 p.m. ET Cleveland Browns @ Pittsburgh Steelers, 1 p.m. ET Atlanta Falcons @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1 p.m. ET Baltimore Ravens @ Buffalo Bills, 1 p.m. ET Minnesota Vikings @ Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET Las Vegas Raiders @ New York Jets, 1 p.m. ET Tennessee Titans @ Cincinnati Bengals, 1 p.m. ET Los Angeles Chargers @ Los Angeles Rams, 4:05 p.m. ET New England Patriots @ Miami Dolphins, 4:25 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs @ Denver Broncos, 4:25 p.m. ET Philadelphia Eagles @ Washington Commanders, 8:20 p.m. ET Monday Chicago Bears @ Seattle Seahawks, 8:15 p.m. ET

articles.title: What does Shedeur Sanders’ rare post mean as Browns reportedly plan to keep him amid trade speculation
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders broke a weeks-long silence on Instagram this week, and the Browns quarterback said nothing with it. No caption.
articles.body: Shedeur Sanders broke a weeks-long silence on Instagram this week, and the Browns quarterback said nothing with it. No caption. Just Mac DeMarco’s “Chamber of Reflection” playing over the post. It arrived with the Nov. 10 trade deadline getting closer and his name still floating around the league. Cleveland reportedly isn’t listening, though. Deshaun Watson has the Browns at 5-2, and Sanders has attempted one pass this season. Whether the post means anything is a guess. The situation around it is easier to read, and it points one way for now.Shedeur Sanders’ rare post lands as Browns reportedly plan to keep himThe post itself is hard to read. Sanders has barely posted this season, yet he rarely leaves the conversation. The NFL recently shared a video of him greeting Titans quarterback Cam Ward after Cleveland’s win on Sunday, even though Sanders never took a snap. That has been the pattern since he entered the league. People talk about him whether he types a word or not.The business side is clearer.According to cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot, the Browns are not shopping Sanders or Gabriel. Another team would need to bring an offer Cleveland could not refuse. That could shift as the deadline nears, but nothing in the reporting suggests a sale is close.Sanders made a move of his own earlier this month. He hired Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports after starting his NFL career without an agent. Adding representation mid-season does not prove he wants out. It does suggest he wants someone watching his options.Outside voices keep pushing the idea. On “UNSPORTSMANLIKE,” ESPN’s Evan Cohen urged the Colts to trade for Sanders and start him. “Shedeur Sanders should be the starting quarterback of the Colts,” Cohen said. “He’s not going to play in Cleveland anytime soon.”Dillon Gabriel’s return makes the quarterback room more crowdedThe Browns activated Gabriel from injured reserve this week. He had been out since a back injury in the preseason. Cleveland now carries Watson, Sanders, Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green on the active roster. Sanders stayed second on Tuesday’s unofficial depth chart, but coach Todd Monken would not lock in the game-day order. Asked Wednesday how Gabriel’s return changes things, he said, “I haven’t gotten there yet.”Not a demotion. Not a promise either.Watson is making the call easier for Cleveland. He threw for 308 yards and ran for a touchdown in the 27-24 win over Tennessee, his first 300-yard game as a Brown. The conversation around him now is about whether he stays beyond this year, not whether Sanders takes over.Sanders started seven games as a rookie, throwing for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. This season he has had almost no chances. Gabriel’s return only adds another option behind Watson, and Cleveland visits Pittsburgh on Sunday. The deadline arrives Nov. 10, which leaves the Browns just under two weeks to decide if any offer beats what they already have.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson's Disappointing Stats Explained by KOC, HC Says Vikings Must 'Activate' Star WR
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell has an explanation for why Justin Jefferson hasn't really gotten going so far this season, while understanding they need to make him more of a focal point in the offense.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell has an explanation for why Justin Jefferson hasn't really gotten going so far this season, while understanding they need to make him more of a focal point in the offense.

Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's practice, O'Connell discussed Minnesota's game script impacting Jefferson's usage as he pointed out a need to "activate" the star receiver:

"In the past we were throwing the ball a thousand times. That's one thing. When you lead the league or you're close to in rushing attempts on the early downs, controlling the game or attempting to control the game, there may not be just the amount of volume [of throws]. But he's our best player. We've got to find a way to continue to activate him."

Javonte Carries Cowboys Back Into Race 😤

Jefferson has 302 receiving yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He leads the Vikings in both categories, but is on pace for his fewest yards and receptions in a full season since entering the NFL.

O'Connell's assessment about the volume of pass attempts impacting Jefferson's usage does track to some extent. The Vikings finished in the top 11 of pass attempts per game every season from 2021 to '23.

Those three seasons mark Jefferson's best in terms of receiving yards per game. He had 3,425 receiving yards across the 2021 and '22 seasons. His 2023 campaign was only 10 games due to a hamstring injury, but he still finished with 1,074 yards.

Since the start of the 2025 season, the Vikings rank 24th in pass attempts per game. Jefferson has 1,350 receiving yards in those 22 games.

However, the outlier here is Jefferson's rookie season in 2020. The Vikings averaged the sixth-fewest pass attempts per game, but he still finished with 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns.

It's hard not to acknowledge that Minnesota's passing game so far this season with Kyler Murray has not taken off. Two of Jefferson's three touchdown catches came in Week 1 with Carson Wentz at quarterback after Murray was injured.

Murray is averaging a career-low 162.4 passing yards per game with just three touchdown passes in five starts.

Despite not getting the full effect of Jefferson's impact, the Vikings are the NFL's last remaining unbeaten team with a 6-0 record thanks to a defense allowing a league-low 12.3 points per game.

Minnesota will look to extend its season-long winning streak to seven games on Sunday in a crucial NFC North showdown with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.

articles.title: Travis Kelce refuses to let Chiefs repeat their mistakes as Broncos clash gives Kansas City a chance to respond
articles.summary: Travis Kelce did not sugarcoat it.
articles.body: Travis Kelce did not sugarcoat it. After the Kansas City Chiefs lost 20-3 to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football, the veteran tight end said the offense has to answer, and soon. Kansas City failed to score a touchdown and never reached the red zone in a game Kelce called another frustrating performance. The Chiefs host the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium at 4:25 p.m. ET, and Kelce says Denver is playing much better than the team Kansas City beat 31-10 in Week 1. He spoke on the October 28 episode of his “New Heights” podcast.Travis Kelce wants the Chiefs offense to fix it fastKansas City played the worst game of Patrick Mahomes’ career, and the numbers back it up. Opta says no NFL offense in the Super Bowl era had gone a game without a touchdown, a run of 10 yards or more and a pass of 20 yards or more while also missing multiple field goals.Kelce was the lone bright spot. Four catches for 44 yards gave him 15,432 receiving yards for a tight end, postseason included, which is a record. He is also fifth all time with 1,104 career receptions. Still, the 37-year-old had little to celebrate.On the podcast, he started with the offense. “Another frustrating performance for the offense,” Kelce said. “I think obviously didn’t even get a chance to get into the red zone…”“We didn’t perform well really on any phase. And it’s gotta fire you the [expletive] up, man. You gotta have a nasty taste in your mouth when you lose.”He was just as direct about what comes next. “I’ll be damned if we go out there and have another [expletive] showing like that again. I can promise you that.”The loss stung more because Kansas City had opened 5-0. “It’s frustrating because we were rolling as a unit for a while there, and I think we’re not far off from getting right back to it,” he said. Kelce named no one, but he wants teammates on time with their routes, releasing cleanly and attacking the defense the right way.Travis Kelce says Denver is playing much better nowThe Broncos lost 31-10 to Kansas City in Week 1, and Kelce expects them to want revenge.“Denver’s playing a lot [expletive] better than they did that first game,” the 11-time Pro Bowler said. “They’ve caught a stride here, and their offense is starting to put up a lot of points.”Denver also gets a key piece back. “They’re getting back (linebacker Jonathon) Cooper, who is a huge part of that pass rush and being stout in that run game. And you know it’s going to be another challenge.”For Kelce, the answer starts inside the building. “I think we need to just learn from this, feel how it felt to get our tail kicked like that, and never let it happen again.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
