articles.title: Caleb Williams not backing down despite NFL fine, says he will continue to wear Caddix cleats
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was fined $11K for wearing Caddix cleats, but he recently explained why that will not deter him from continuing to w...
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was fined $11K for wearing Caddix cleats, but he recently explained why that will not deter him from continuing to wear them.

Caleb Williams was fined $11,941 by the NFL for displaying the Caddix logo on his cleats during the Chicago Bears' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Although he wore the cleats again in Week 7, no fine has been issued for that transgression at the moment.

Williams appealed the fine, arguing the cleats help him stay healthy. The QB has no endorsement deal with Caddix but plans to keep wearing the cleats, even if it means further fines. The company has said it will cover the penalties. The Bears star recently spoke up about why he has made this decision.

Caleb Williams explains how Caddix cleats help 'take tension off' his joints and tendons

A fairly new athletic footwear brand, Caddix has a patented SmartStuds technology which allows the studs on the sole to flex and release under pressure. This helps reduce rotational force on the knees and ankles during sudden turns and changes of direction, which explains why NFL stars might be big fans.

Williams explained all of this and more to the press in detail when asked about it recently.

"They are a science-type of cleat. It's something that focuses on when you plant on the hard plants on turf or grass, they call them SmartStuds, and they move when you move. They take tension off of your tendons, your joints and all of that… I'm focused on being able to be out here for the guys. And if that can give me a small percentage up and it works, then that's what I'm gonna do."

If the cleats become something more NFL stars are embracing, then perhaps the league might partner up with them, but that remains to be seen. It seems that both Williams and the company are locked in at the moment, with fines not particularly a concern to either.

articles.title: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
articles.summary: The Broncos and Chiefs square off on a huge AFC West game.
articles.body:
For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback.

The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs were 12-0. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. Then the season opener was like old times.

It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage as he ran through many missed tackles by the Broncos for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance.

It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. Denver's defense has played much better since that weird off night at Kansas City, however.

While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. They're 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs and that's to take Walker out of the game, but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season:

There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict.

The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time. But they are probably the better team. Certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time.

The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back. But what about Dallas' defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Cowboys laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30.

Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll.

Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week.

It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly.

You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. Their remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good.

If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until mid-fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal.

The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog.

Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season. But they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers.

It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest.

A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better.

The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes nuts against a questionable Bears defense. It should be a good game, and if that holds it'll be nice to have the underdog.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals, Dallas Cowboys share 5 player connections
articles.summary: The Cardinals have some former Cowboys, and the Cowboys have some former Cardinals as they face each other in Week 8.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals face the Dallas Cowboys this week on the road. They faced each other just a season ago. At one time, they were division rivals.

When the two teams meet on Sunday, there will be some reunions of sorts.

There are a few player connections between the two teams. The Cardinals have two former Cowboys players on their team. The Cowboys have three former Cardinals, although none is currently on their 53-man roster.

They had a fourth, but running back Emari Demercado was cut this week and claimed by the Houston Texans .

Who are the Cardinals-Cowboys player connections?

Fehoko is in his second season with the Cardinals. He was drafted by the Cowboys in the fifth round in 2021 and played 10 games over two seasons for the Cowboys.

Kreiter never played in an NFL game for Dallas, but he signed with them as a rookie free agent in 2014 after he went undrafted.

Thompson is on injured reserve but has begun practicing. He joined the Cowboys this offseason as a free agent on a three-year contract. He played seven seasons for the Cardinals and was drafted by them in the 2019 supplemental draft.

Bullard is a well traveled vet. He is also on injured reserve but designated to return. He played for the Cardinals in 2019, appearing in nine games before he got hurt. He had 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks for the Cardinals.

Leverett is on Dallas' practice squad. He spent parts of two seasons (2024-2025) on the Cardinals' practice squad and active roster. He played one game for the Cardinals in 2024.

articles.title: What Commanders QB Jayden Daniels wants to improve coming out of bye
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels has spoken to OC David Blough about how Commanders can be more efficient heading into Eagles clash
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels has been scrutinized more that he's used to this past week, with his play under the microscope during a bye and blame being freely cast his way. Such is life when you're 1-4-1 .

It's common for NFL quarterbacks on underperforming teams, but not something he has experienced since being taken No. 2 overall in the 2024 NFL draft. The man was darn near invincible during his rookie year , when the Commanders went to the NFC title game and he was named offensive rookie of the year. Daniels might've had the best rookie season ever for a quarterback, when Washington went 8-4 in one-score games.

Daniels has battled through another left elbow dislocation. There are times this season where he has been that dude, especially since returning from injury. He was awesome in the second half versus San Francisco, but that throwaway on fourth down raised an eyebrow. He was darn near great against the Giants, right up until the fateful end where he had a brain fart that led to a Week 5 tie .

The bye week naturally leads to reflection, especially the results we've described. What can Jayden do better? Well, a lot. That's especially true while operating David Blough's new system , which requires more under center work and pre-snap adjustments and thinking overall.

"Having urgency in and out of the huddle is the biggest thing for me, where I can grow even more," Daniels said during a Wednesday press conference . "It's getting up to the line of scrimmage and giving us more time to dissect and have an idea of what the defense is presenting and what they're doing. That's the biggest thing, the communication in and out of the huddle."

Daniels has talked to Blough about that. They've got a collaborative relationship that isn't new, even with Blough's promotion to offensive coordinator after years as assistant quarterbacks coach.

"He's very receptive to everything I talk about," Daniels said. "He's always asking me what I like and what I don't like. That's the relationship that we've built. He's a first-time coordinator but he's been here for three years so we've built that rapport. We have a common goal in that we want to win and we want to put our best foot forward."

That starts on Sunday night against the Philadelphia Eagles in a virtual must-win situation for Washington. Daniels has some real positive stats out there in terms of turnover worth plays.

That's a good thing. But not when you're losing. When you're 1-4-1 and have made some costly blunders, this stat morphs into an argument that Daniels isn't being aggressive enough. Such is life for a high-profile individual playing the most important position in the most popular sport.

Head coach Dan Quinn admitted there's a fine balance for Daniels, finding accuracy and being smart with the football while still pushing for more. He's learning that, with a bunch of voices rattling around in his head trying to adjust to a new system while trying to avoid injury and negative plays. He's a work in progress, with tons of room left to grow. He's also battling his own standard, set in that illustrious 2024 campaign.

"I'm constantly my biggest critic, win, lose or draw," Daniels said. "…There are always plays that I left out there in addition to the plays that I made. You just try to minimize that gap."

He must do so right away, with this Eagles game crucial to a run Washington must go on to re-join the NFC East race.

"We have to put a complete game together," Daniels said. "We have yet to do that."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes vs Micah Parsons - why ACL recovery timelines differ
articles.summary: On December 14, 2025, Micah Parsons and Patrick Mahomes both suffered ACL injuries just hours apart.
articles.body: On December 14, 2025, Micah Parsons and Patrick Mahomes both suffered ACL injuries just hours apart. Patrick is back on the gridiron, leading his team, the Kansas City Chiefs, to six wins and one loss, while Micah still remains on the PUP [Physically Unable to Perform] list.Sports orthopedic surgeon Dr. Michael J. Alaia explains why the two NFL players have experienced different recovery timelines. “The fans always want to know, ‘Why is it taking so long?’ When you do enough ACLs, you just know the variability of the recovery can be so vast.And every patient brings their own set of physical and psychological needs.” So, does that mean Patrick is psychologically and physically stronger than Micah? Not necessarily. Maybe it does. But still, let’s find out what truly counts.Micah Parsons’ ACL injury and meniscus repair delayed his NFL returnMicah Parsons was initially expected to return by Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys. However, he missed that game and Week 7 and is now set to miss Week 8 vs. Carolina Panthers as well.According to an ESPN source familiar with Parsons’ recovery, a November return was always the most likely scenario. “It was the only thing that made sense knowing he wanted to be 100%.Micah has to play a different game than most guys and relies on his speed and athleticism - on top of the fact that he had the meniscus tear, which made it a longer recovery period.When he wasn’t going to practice at all in training camp, it solidified where he was at in his recovery process.” Parsons’ surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, performed a full meniscus repair, which has significantly extended his recovery timeline.Why Patrick Mahomes recovered faster than Micah ParsonsDr. Sharif Tabbah, who has worked with several NFL players recovering from ACL injuries, explained how a full meniscus repair can complicate rehabilitation.“When it’s a repair, you’re not allowed to bend your knee past 90 degrees for between 4 to 8 weeks, depending on the surgeon’s call. So that obviously leads to a lot of stiffness and gives guys a hard time getting back into that deep knee bend, which even positionally could make a big difference.”Micah Parsons told ESPN this week that he did not walk without assistance for 8 weeks, whereas many ACL patients begin walking without crutches within 2 weeks. His full meniscus repair may therefore be a major factor in his slower recovery process, as protecting the repaired tissue is of prime importance.Patrick Mahomes, on the other hand, had no reported meniscus issues. He suffered an LCL tear that required immediate surgery.Parsons’ surgery was delayed partly because he was awaiting the birth of his third child and partly because doctors wanted the swelling to subside before operating. The surgery was only one part of the process; recovery and rehabilitation created unpredictable turns.Parsons reached out to Dr. Sharif Tabbah immediately after his injury and expressed an interest in working together during his recovery. “We stayed in touch throughout the process. He sent me some videos and updates. I gave him some guidance along the way from afar. But he never actually ended up coming.”Tucker Kraft returned faster from ACL tearAs per Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft, who tore his right ACL in November 2025, “Every ACL recovery is different. [Micah Parsons] had a little bit more work done.So his surgeon held him back from full weight-bearing and running a little while longer. It’s just different. And that’s something he’ll overcome very soon.”Tucker Kraft returned to practice 8 and a half months after his surgery. He was cleared for full team drills 2 and a half weeks later. He made his season debut in Week 1. He did take a hit to his leg in Week 6 and was checked in the medical tent but he quickly returned to the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Opponent Breakdown: Stanford Cardinal Defense
articles.summary: Stanford’s new staff is heavy on NFL experience, and that is very clear at the defensive coordinator position. Kris Richard was a solid NFL player who worked...
articles.body:
Stanford's new staff is heavy on NFL experience, and that is very clear at the defensive coordinator position. Kris Richard was a solid NFL player who worked his way through the coaching ranks in the league as a position coach and coordinator. He heads to college this year to lead this defense, with improving results as the season goes on.

While the defense has shown signs of improvement, they are limited by the play up front along the defensive line. The group as a whole has produced one more sack than Clev Lubin, while also putting up 16 tackles for loss, which is about the combined amount of three defensive linemen for the Cards. The comparison on those stats is notable, but Louisville has done a poor job of keeping opposing defenses out of the backfield this season. They are one of the worst teams in the country at allowing negative plays, and they can't let this defensive line take advantage of that.

Matt Rose is one of the best linebackers in the country, but he has not played in four straight games, so the Cards may not have to worry about him. Rose is third on the team in tackles while leading the team in tackles for loss. He has not played in a game in over a month. The impact that Rose has on this defense can't be overstated, and it's up in the air whether he will play in this game. The other linebackers on this roster have just not been able to make the types of plays that Rose does. The defense gave up 115 points in the first two games after Rose's injury. They were much better against NC State, but it remains to be seen if that game was a fluke.

The Cardinal has one of the worst pass defenses in the country, with 17 touchdowns thrown against them and multiple other statistics ranked in the 90s or worse in the country. The Cardinal have done a solid job of avoiding explosive plays in most of their games, but Wake Forest, Notre Dame, and Miami put up video game numbers in the pass game against them. Louisville has one of the most explosive offenses in the country, so this should be an opportunity to do the same.

articles.title: ‘He hates him’ – NFL fans think Patrick Mahomes is upset after Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes addressed the organisation’s decision to sign kicker Justin Tucker. Tucker spent the first 10 weeks of the 2025 NFL sea...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes addressed the organisation's decision to sign kicker Justin Tucker.

Tucker spent the first 10 weeks of the 2025 NFL season under suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy over allegations of inappropriate conduct during massage sessions between 2012 and 2016.

While the Baltimore Ravens ended Tucker's 12-year tenure with the franchise, and he has remained unsigned since, the Chiefs have taken the bold step of offering Tucker a roster spot by adding him to their practice squad.

Patrick Mahomes reacts to Chiefs signing Justin Tucker

Mahomes spoke about the Chiefs signing Tucker after practice on October 28, sharing a pretty flat and professional response.

"Yeah, we have a lot of people that are added in and out. I try not to get too high or too low on anything. I know Veach does a great job bringing great players in. But for me, it is about the Denver Broncos, moving on, and continuing to get better because we have a lot of stuff to clean up."

With Mahomes giving a tepid reaction to Tucker's signing, fans are already pointing out how this is not like the 31-year-old QB and how his actual feelings for the kicker are shining through in his responses.

"He hates him; never saw Mahomes not being excited for someone new," observed one fan .

"I've never seen Patrick Mahomes NOT say 'excited to have him on our football team' until they signed Justin Tucker. This is Patrick Mahomes 'I hate that dude' speak and body language," said another fan, thinking Mahomes is unhappy with this signing .

"Pat's been working on his poker face. Respect," said a fan .

"Yeah, he don't mess with him," said another fan .

"Omg he is not happy about this!! He has never had this middle-ground reaction about someone coming in. Please, the Chiefs are an unserious organisation," criticised one fan .

The Chiefs signed Tucker because of the struggles starting kicker Harrison Butker has faced, going 11-for-16 on field goal attempts this season. Tucker's career record is 417-for-468 on field goal attempts, for a total conversion percentage of 89.1%, which makes him an appealing option.

The Chiefs are 5-1 this NFL season and among the leading Super Bowl contenders, so this move is a high-risk gamble to potentially upgrade the production they are getting at kicker, even if it means making a very unpopular signing.

articles.title: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 things to watch for in Week 8
articles.summary: Here are five things to watch for on the field during the Jets' Week 8 game vs. the Raiders.
articles.body:
The New York Jets host the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium as part of the NFL's Week 8 offering. Both teams are looking to halt a slide. New York enters at 2-5 after consecutive losses, while Las Vegas is 3-4 following four straight defeats after opening their season 3-0.

This is a game the Jets should be able to win all things considered.

Then again, that's the same thing we said about Week 7's divisional clash with the Miami Dolphins . Even still, this game feels winnable for the home team.

Here are five things Jets Wire will be watching as New York tries to end its two-game skid.

How engaged will the MetLife Stadium crowd be?

Fans were upset after New York handed the previously winless Dolphins their first victory of the season . It's easy to see why. Week 7 set up favorably for the Jets to do some damage. Now, rather than enjoy some positive atmosphere, they're trying to stop the bleeding.

The crowd's response could depend heavily on how the Jets start. An early scoring drive or a defensive stop would give the home team a chance to bring the energy back into the building, while another slow start could make a difficult afternoon even more uncomfortable. New York needs to give its fans a reason to believe the game will be different from the previous two.

Aaron Glenn is going to maintain his positivity . That we know. None of his players are going to exhibit negative traits to the media, but the body language in that Week 7 game was troubling. It will be interesting to see what type of energy is displayed on the sideline in this one.

There is a difference between frustration after losing and a locker room that has stopped believing in its leadership. Demario Davis has defended the team's character and resilience, while Dane Belton has pointed to the opportunity the Jets still have to improve. Their comments offer a counterpoint to the perception that the team is coming apart, but the next test is whether that belief shows up in the way the Jets respond to adversity against Las Vegas.

The Kirk Cousins vs. Geno Smith quarterback duel

Two grisly old vets that entered the NFL with expectations and promise. Both have evolved into savvy veterans that their teammates always seem to play hard for. Both can do some nice things. Both have enjoyed decent careers. Neither is going to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Who takes the edge in this one?

Cousins enters the matchup with a significant statistical advantage in touchdown production. He leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes through seven games, while Smith has thrown 10 touchdowns and two interceptions. Cousins remains Las Vegas' starter despite the Raiders ' losing streak, and the Jets must find a way to disrupt his rhythm rather than letting him dictate the game from the pocket.

Smith, meanwhile, needs to avoid the costly mistakes that have hurt New York in recent weeks. If he protects the football and takes advantage of the opportunities the Raiders' defense presents, the Jets could have a chance to win the quarterback matchup even if Cousins produces another productive outing.

A chess match between Aaron Glenn and Klint Kubiak

Aaron Glenn can earn himself some positive press in this one if he can outwit Klint Kubiak in their chess match. Glenn calls plays for the Jets offense. Klint Kubiak calls the offensive plays for the Las Vegas Raiders offense. A Jets team that has had difficulty scoring will need to put up points, but it would help if Glenn can keep the Raiders from doing the same. They have scored 21 points or more in all of their games but one, and they have scored 26 points or more five times

For New York, the challenge is finding a way to slow down an offense that has continued to score despite the team's losing streak. The Jets cannot afford to let Las Vegas dictate the tempo, particularly if they struggle to finish drives themselves. Defensive adjustments and situational decisions will matter, especially if the Raiders find early success and force New York to chase the scoreboard.

Which team does the better job of handling adversity?

The Jets are 2-5 on the season and third in the AFC East. The Raiders have a better record (3-4) but have lost four straight after beginning the season at 3-0. Both sides are handling adversity. Both sides will experience adversity. The team that does the better job will probably end its losing streak.

The Raiders' losing streak has come despite Cousins' productive passing numbers, while the Jets have struggled to find consistency across all three phases. Neither team can afford to let one setback turn into several, and the response after a mistake could be just as important as the opening game plan. For New York, that means staying composed if the Raiders score early and making sure frustration does not dictate the next decision.

articles.title: Sacks don’t tell full story for Jaguars’ Josh Hines-Allen
articles.summary: It’s not a surprise fans want to finally see a team that gets home, however, the sacks, or lack thereof, don’t tell the whole story in Anthony Campanile’s de...
articles.body:
The main criticism for Josh Hines-Allen, and the Jaguars' pass-rush on the whole, is the lack of sack production. The unit has ranked 24th, 29th, 30th, 27th, and 28th in sack % over the last five years

It's not a surprise fans want to finally see a team that gets home, however, the sacks, or lack thereof, don't tell the whole story in Anthony Campanile's defense.

Josh Hines-Allen and the Jaguars' pass-rush is actually doing more heavy lifting than many fans decide According to the NFL's NextGenStats, the Jaguars pressure opposing quarterbacks the fastest on average of any team (2.44s) and at the eighth highest rate (39.1%). Unfortunately, the opposing quarterback is getting the ball out quicker than any other team (3.06s) than any other team.

The Jaguars also flash the fastest get-off in the league at just 0.77s and it's Josh Hines-Allen who is the Jaguars' quickest to pressure. He is tied for the most quick pressures on the team (7) and has one of the fastest get-offs.

The sacks aren't there, but the impact is. The Jaguars have forced the second-most turnovers off pressure. That said, the impact of sacks can't be understated. There's no way around it, they are simply drive killers, in most defenses that is.

Josh Hines-Allen is statistically having about the worst season of his career as a pass-rusher.

This year, his pressure rate sits right at 9.8%, where his previous season-worst was 11.7% in his injury-shortened 2020 season. He's on pace for just over four sacks this season.

But, both NextGenStats and Pro Football Focus believe his actual pass-rushing success is far greater than these numbers might indicate. His pass-rush win rate ranks 10th and 22nd among edge-rushers, respectively, between the two datasets. Teams are getting the ball out so quickly, it's rare they get a true chance to sack the quarterback.

The Jaguars rank as the NFL's best run-defense for the second straight season and Hines-Allen's impact on the edge is a big reason as to why. As a run-defender, he's among the best in the NFL.

Hines-Allen's 11.5% run-stop % ranks third at the position and Travon Walker isn't too far behind at 15th (7.5%). The impact of those two as edge-setters is among the league's best kept secrets. It's why the Jaguars are the best run-defense team in the league.

The truth is, the Hines-Allen and the Jags are doing precisely what Campanile wants, and it's working. Force teams to become one-dimensional, make them uncomfortable in the pocket, and the mistakes will come.

Fans might not be happy that the sacks aren't there, but the turnovers are. As a result, the Jaguars are third in points per game (17.3) and, truthfully, that's all that really matters. This week Daniel Jones comes to town, tied for the NFL-lead in turnovers.

articles.title: Rams anticipate Davante Adams back sooner than later
articles.summary: Davante Adams is reportedly recovering quickly and more NFL news on a Wednesday
articles.body:
Sean McVay reported that Davante Adams had a successful surgery , and as far as the head coach is aware, Adams could be back closer to six weeks from now than 10. Adams being back healthy and sooner than later would be good news for L.A.

Six to 10 weeks was the projected time Adams would be out with his hamstring injury . If he missed the full 10 weeks his season would be in jeopardy . While six weeks missed could have Adams rejoining the Rams at a very important stretch of the season. The Rams have to keep winning to make Adams comeback all the more relevant.

Hopefully for Adams and the Rams, his recovery continues to trend in a positive way. Of course, the Rams have plenty of other players are on the mend as well. Can the Rams keep their season afloat while players like Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman and more recover?

The Rams, ready or not, play again this Sunday. They will have to hope they are healed enough to win by then.

"McVay told reporters Wednesday that Adams will probably return "closer to the shorter term" of the 6-to-10-week timeline , which means he could be back in the mix shortly after the team's Week 11 bye. Adams ruptured his hamstring in Week 6 against the Cardinals and underwent surgery on it recently.

Adams already missed last week's game against the Raiders , which was his first of the season. He's required to miss at least three more while on injured reserve."

"We will not start Myles' or Terrance Ferguson's clock this week," McVay said.

Garrett has been out since undergoing knee surgery after the team's Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The Rams never gave a firm timetable for his return, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported it was a six-week timeline . This will now be Garrett's seventh missed game, so his recovery is taking longer than expected.

McVay even admitted that he knows "it's frustrating."

"Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett will reportedly not practice this week per "The NFL Report."

"With each passing week, it seems the Los Angeles Rams suffer a new injury and share disappointing news on Myles Garrett. That held true again this week, though there are some glimmers of hope.

While Garrett and Ferguson won't return this week , Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman are both trending up. McDuffie will be a limited participant on Wednesday, while Landman has cleared the concussion protocol and will be a full participant.

Coleman Shelton will miss practice due to a hip injury, and Colby Parkinson is also being held out because of a rib injury. Sean McVay said Joe Cardona has an ankle injury , which will cause him to miss Wednesday's practice."

"The Rams (3-4) signed long snapper Jake McQuaide to the practice squad after Joe Cardona injured his ankle early in Sunday's victory over the Las Vegas Raiders . Cardona did not practice on Wednesday as he nursed the injury. McQuaide, 38, returned to the Rams for a second stint last season after spending the first 10 years of his career with the franchise. He was brought in to replace Alex Ward after the field goal unit struggled with its consistency. The kicker who was replaced simultaneously with Ward last year was Josh Karty. articles.title: NFL Week 8 Survivor/Eliminator Picks
articles.summary: The Chargers were 9.5-point favorites against the Cardinals in Week 1, and they were at home. The Seahawks were 8.5-point favorites against the Commanders in...
articles.body:
The Chargers were 9.5-point favorites against the Cardinals in Week 1, and they were at home. The Seahawks were 8.5-point favorites against the Commanders in Week 3. They were on the road, but then the Commanders had their backup quarterback on the field. The Texans were 9.5-point favorites against the Giants in Week 7, and they were at home. All three lost. Also, all three were my NFL Survivor picks for that week. This isn't to defend myself, exactly, but I refuse to say the picks I made were bad picks. They should have won, dammit. But they didn't. If you followed me so far … well, whoopsie. But let's clean slate it now. Perfect from here on. That's the goal. Check out my Week 8 pick for Survivor contests. And while we're here, you can use our NFL Betting Model and our Bet Tracker to make a pick for yourself.

Every week, we have the same process. We eliminate teams in groups until we narrow it down to our real considerations. Start with all 32, whittle it down. And remember — this game is "once you use a team, they're off the board," so it's not always just a matter of taking the team you think will win. There has to be some strategy. I can't pick a team I've picked before, but you might not have tailed me, so previously used teams are eligible until the end.

My favorite category — picks I can't get wrong! If you don't play, you can't win, but also I won't pick you, so woohoo for easy. (I clearly need the help.) Houston Texans New Orleans Saints New York Giants San Francisco 49ers That's four off the board.

Maybe these are good teams, maybe not, but it's too hard to trust them given who they are facing. This is a 10-team list every week (fewer when there are byes); we are eliminating anyone facing a top-10 team in our FTN NFL Power Rankings . Baltimore Ravens (@ Buffalo) Chicago Bears (@ Seattle) Denver Broncos (vs. Kansas City) Detroit Lions (vs. Minnesota) Indianapolis Colts (@ Jacksonville) Kansas City Chiefs (@ Denver) Los Angeles Chargers (@ LA Rams) Seattle Seahawks (vs. Chicago) Tennessee Titans (@ Cincinnati) Some of these teams will win but you can't confidently say so, considering who they're facing. That's nine more gone, 19 to go.

You can face the worst team in all of football, but if you're the second-worst team, well, I'm still not going to be too excited about selecting you. We'll return to the power rankings here and cross off any team in the bottom 12. Arizona Cardinals (@ Dallas) Atlanta Falcons (@ Tampa Bay) Las Vegas Raiders (@ NY Jets) Miami Dolphins (vs. New England) New York Jets (vs. Las Vegas) Philadelphia Eagles (@ Washington) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (vs. Atlanta) Washington Commanders (vs. Philadelphia Eight more eliminations leaves us with 11 remaining.

Island games just get weird. I would need some very convincing evidence to pick anyone on a Thursday, or a Monday, or an overseas 9:30 a.m. ET game. There aren't many left this week, but I still want to note them. Carolina Panthers (@ Green Bay) Green Bay Packers (vs. Carolina) Two more gone, nine left. But this week, we have one extra category.

There are plenty of teams over .500 this week, enough that teams can be over .500, look good and still not be in the top 10 in our power rankings. And this week, some of them play each other. So even if they aren't necessarily among the best teams, I don't much think they're worth my mental energy. Divisional matchup, good team, scary situation. Cleveland Browns (@ Pittsburgh) Minnesota Vikings (@ Detroit) Pittsburgh Steelers (vs. Cleveland) And that's three more gone, leaving us with six teams — our seven contenders.

Once we're down to this small a number of teams, we're done cutting them in swaths. We look at the pros and cons for each team and then figure it out. I'm also diving into our NFL Betting Model to see what the numbers think of the game.

Model Projection : Bills 27.34-25.38, Bills 55.1% win rate Pros : The Bills are coming off a bye and are pretty healthy, while Lamar Jackson is still banged up on the other side. Cons : We expect Jackson to be back, and this is as much a rivalry game as any divisional matchup right now.

Model Projection : Bengals 26.80-21.70, Bengals 62.9% win rate Pros : The Bengals have taken their game to a new level this year. The Titans have not done that. Cons : Maybe you want to save the Bengals for later? Or (like me) you used them already?

Model Projection : Cowboys 30.23-24.35, Cowboys 63.2% win rate Pros : The Dallas offense was really clicking against Philadelphia, and Arizona's defense isn't any great shakes itself. Cons : Dallas' defense can let you down against pretty much anyone.

Model Projection : Jaguars 26.93-20.82, Jaguars 65.6% win rate Pros : The Jags are a very good team coming off a bye and without many injury concerns. The Colts are terrible and now in fire-sale mode. Cons : The Jags still have two games against Tennessee, a game against Washington and another Colts game on the slate. Might be prudent to save them.

Model Projection : Rams 29.65-19.11, Rams 75.0% win rate Pros : There is one Los Angeles team worth a crap right now, and it's the Rams. Cons : Eventually injuries catch up with everyone (see the 49ers last week). The Chargers are terrible, so it's hard to see a path, but if the Rams just get too hurt?

Model Projection : Patriots 26.20-21.70, Patriots 61.6% win rate Pros : New England is a contender. Miami is a contender for the first overall pick. Cons : The Pats swept the Dolphins last year, but before that, they had lost four straight, eight of nine and 11 of 15 to their division foes. It's a squirrelly matchup.

Listen, I'm not having a good year. I'm taking one I feel like I can count on. There's no real way the Jags lose this game. There are a few matchups in Week 8 I feel that way about, but I stand by the idea that there's no real way the Jags lose this one. The truth is, though, that there are several good choices this week. You could have a good time delving into the honorable mentions this time around.

articles.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson reportedly expected to return in Week 8 after missing 3 games with a high ankle sprain
articles.summary: Jackson has been out since suffering the injury in Week 4 against the Titans.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are expected to get quarterback Lamar Jackson back for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports .

Jackson has missed the Ravens' past three games after suffering a high ankle sprain against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. The quarterback returned to practice last week in a limited capacity before being ruled out for the Ravens' Week 7 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

After returning to the field this week as a full practice participant, Jackson is poised to make his return on Sunday — barring a setback.

"The more you're able to do and respond from and feel from certainly raises your optimism," said Ravens head coach Jesse Minter when asked if Jackson was trending toward playing in Week 8.

Jackson explained last week that the biggest factor in whether he would be able to play was not so much the level of swelling but how much of the pain he could deal with.

Jackson's importance to the roster is on display every time he takes the field. According to ESPN's Jamison Hensley , the Ravens have scored 14 touchdowns in the 14 quarters the quarterback has played this season. In the 14 quarters without Jackson, Baltimore has only found the end zone five times.

"He's the leader of this offense, so anytime he's out there, it's always great," said running back Derrick Henry . "I know he wants to be out there with us and to put us in the best position to win. He wants the guys to play great as well. So, I'll be excited whenever he's back out there, and I look forward to it."

Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson over the past three weeks, leading the Ravens to a 1-2 record.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Reveals Trade Request Stance Amid Colts' Fire Sale, Rumors Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Despite the Indianapolis Colts initiating a fire sale this week, superstar running back Jonathan Taylor is not looking to push his way out of the organization.
articles.body:
Despite the Indianapolis Colts initiating a fire sale this week, superstar running back Jonathan Taylor is not looking to push his way out of the organization.

According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Taylor said Thursday that he has not requested a trade, although Taylor also acknowledged that he doesn't have "full control of his future."

Taylor offered additional comments on where things stand with him, telling reporters that he is proud to be a member of the Colts.

"I haven't heard anything, and I can't control that, obviously. You guys know that I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. And similar to Quenton [Nelson] and [DeForest Buckner], they were proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. So, hopefully that day may not come. But I can't control that.

"The only thing I can control is corralling these guys in the locker room, helping us put together a great plan, and executing a great play for Jacksonville—because, like I said, it's a division game. They're licking their chops right now, they think they're going to kick us while we're down, and that has to be a point of emphasis. So, we've got to just take it day-by-day."

On Tuesday, the 2-5 Colts made two huge moves, trading guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-round selection, and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-rounder.

Amid the Colts moving on from other key players, Taylor has naturally come up in trade rumors and speculation in recent days.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that although there is "heavy interest" in Taylor, teams "aren't totally sold" on the idea of the Colts trading him, and he "isn't a slam dunk" to get moved.

Indy signed Taylor to a two-year, $44 million extension in August, meaning he is under contract through the 2028 season.

As a result, the Colts don't necessarily have to feel any pressure to trade Taylor, even if it is clear that they are looking past this season and into the future.

If the Colts have designs on bouncing back next season and getting back in the playoff mix, then Taylor figures to be a huge part of that process.

The 27-year-old Taylor is the Colts' best offensive player and the face of the franchise, meaning there would be bigger implications behind trading him than there were for Nelson or Buckner.

A three-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro, Taylor is trending toward yet another great season, having rushed for 587 yards and eight touchdowns, while also catching 17 passes for 178 yards through seven games.

Taylor is also coming off two hugely productive seasons, rushing for 1,431 yards and 11 touchdowns in 2024, as well as 1,585 yards and 18 touchdowns last season.

For a running back of his caliber, teams would likely be willing to give up a significant package of draft picks.

Most running backs don't garner a first-round pick in this day and age, but Taylor is a supreme talent and a difference-maker, so that may be what the Colts are holding out for.

Taylor is showing no signs of slowing down, though, and appears to be firmly in his prime, so the Colts may view him as a foundational piece who can continue to be a key contributor for years to come.

The Colts' stance will become clearer over the next couple of weeks, as the NFL trade deadline is on Nov. 10.

articles.title: NFL Insider Says 'All Hell Is Going to Break Loose' amid Rumors Ahead of Trade Deadline
articles.summary: NFL general managers are reportedly anticipating an active trade deadline after some major October moves.
articles.body:
NFL general managers are reportedly anticipating an active trade deadline after some major October moves.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Thursday that "after talking to several NFL teams and GMs over the last hour, my expectation is the trade deadline will be even crazier than anticipated."

According to Schultz, one source told him: "All hell is going to break loose over the next week and a half. Get your popcorn ready."

Schultz predicted the Chicago Bears' decision to give up two first-round picks to acquire Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans "will cause other teams to react and try to be bold as well."

Simmons is the latest major name to move ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline following the Indianapolis Colts' decision to trade guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.

The Seattle Seahawks gave up a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder to acquire Nelson, while the San Francisco 49ers shipped out a 2027 fourth-rounder in order to grab Buckner.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported there have been 18 trades between Oct. 1 and the trade deadline in each of the last two years.

The 2026 lead-up to the deadline could exceed that trend. The Dallas Cowboys' trade for Joey Porter Jr., the Baltimore Ravens' acquisition of Cam Jurgens and the Houston Texans' deal for Marvin Harrison Jr. mean there have already been six deals made since the start of the month.

Last year, it was the New York Jets making a splash at the deadline by trading Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner. This year it could be both the Titans (1-6) and Colts (2-5) making more moves ahead of the deadline.

Titans safety Amani Hooker joins Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs on Bleacher Report's trade block big board heading into Week 8.

The Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) are another likely seller, which is why edge rusher Khalil Mack currently sits at the top of the B/R big board.

Other top B/R trade candidates include Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings and Miami Dolphins defensive lineman Zach Sieler as well as Philadelphia Eagles guard Landon Dickerson and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler recently named Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Yaya Diaby, Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne, Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen and Cardinals safety Budda Baker as other potential trade candidates ahead of the deadline.

How Week 8 plays out will impact some potential sellers that could be still on the fence as to which direction to take at the deadline. The Buccaneers, for example, will see their NFL Next Gen Stats playoff odds jump to 30 percent with a Sunday win over the visiting Atlanta Falcons but plummet to just 11 percent with a loss.
